title: What is LGS1920 Studio?
description: A plain-language introduction to LGS1920 Studio, its workflow, its exports, and what you need to get started.

hero.title: What is Studio, and what can you do with it?
hero.lead: Studio is a privacy-first browser workspace for turning an existing outdoor route into a clear map presentation and a shareable video. Add POIs, choose camera views, adjust map layers and widgets, and keep your work local in your browser by default.

sectionNav.summary: Four steps from file to export

sectionNav.label: What it creates
sectionNav.summary: Video for social networks, snapshots, and reports

overview.title: Your route, organized and enriched in one browser workspace.
intro: Studio opens directly in your browser. Import an existing route file, view it on a 2D or 3D map, and prepare a clear presentation of the journey without a paid subscription.

Adjust the route, add points of interest and useful information, choose what the camera shows, and prepare a replay for a shareable video. Snapshots and reports remain available when you prefer a still or documentary format. Studio is used after or around an outing; it does not record the activity while you are outdoors.
overview.simpleIntro: Start with the defaults, then refine the map, camera, POIs, colors and widgets as far as your story requires.

basics.title: Start with a route file
basics.body: Load a GeoJSON, GPX, or KML file created by a GPS device, a mobile application, another mapping tool, or one of the Studio samples.

basics.title: Explore and prepare the 3D scene
basics.body: Inspect the route on the map, switch layers, change its appearance, add context, and prepare the view without installing a traditional desktop editor.

basics.title: Prepare and share a video
basics.body: Add POIs, change map layers, add colors, and choose different widgets. Everything remains editable to suit your needs. Record and share the result on your social networks.

items.title: Private by default
items.body: Your work stays in your browser by default.
items.note: Local synchronization across devices is already possible. A future version may also support your own cloud storage.

items.title: Free today and tomorrow
items.body: Studio is free to use today and will remain free.
items.note: Some external map or data services may be paid by their own providers. Studio offers them to enrich your videos but has no commercial relationship of any kind with those providers.

workflow.title: A session in four steps.
workflow.intro: You do not need to know every tool before starting. A first session can follow this simple order.

steps.title: Open or import a route
steps.body: Choose a sample or load a GeoJSON, GPX, or KML file from your device.

steps.title: Check the journey
steps.body: Make sure the route, tracks, and points of interest appear in the right place.

steps.title: Prepare the presentation
steps.body: Choose the map layers, colors, camera view, POIs, replay, widgets, and any text or statistics you want to show.

steps.title: Record and share
steps.body: Replay the journey, record the video, then share it on your social networks or download it. Snapshots and reports remain available when needed.

outputs.title: The main result: a video you can share.
outputs.intro: The video workflow is the main way to present a journey. Reports remain available when a document is more useful.

items.title: Video for social networks
items.body: Replay the journey and record the map scene, camera movement, and visible widgets. Export the result for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or another social network.

items.title: Reports
items.body: Generate a PDF document or a packaged HTML report with route information, statistics, points of interest, and maps.

practical.title: A few useful things to know.
practical.intro: Studio is designed to be opened and tried directly. These points explain the main technical requirements without requiring specialist knowledge.

items.title: Your working data stays local by default
items.body: Route files and the current project are handled in the browser unless you explicitly use a synchronization or external service.

items.title: Use a recent browser
items.body: The map needs WebGL. Video work can use more memory, so closing unused tabs may make recording smoother.

items.title: Free today and tomorrow
items.body:
Studio is free to use today and will remain free to use. There is no paid plan, subscription, or activation fee. Studio gives you access to more than 30 free basemaps.
Unlike many other apps, video creation is completely free, with no limits other than those of your device.

items.title: Optional freemium or paid assets
items.body:
You can also use external map and data assets from freemium or paid providers, such as Cesium (Google 3D, Google Maps, etc.), MapTiler, and more.
These services are optional and billed by their own providers. Studio offers them to enrich your videos but has no commercial relationship of any kind with these providers.

privacyQuote.title: Your privacy comes first.
privacyQuote.text: With Studio, you don’t need to create an online account to access your data. We don’t track you, so use the app however you like.
privacyQuote.rule: The only rule is: have fun using it—and please keep the credits visible. Thank you.

basic.title: What is LGS1920 Studio?
basic.intro: Studio helps you turn an existing outdoor route into a replay and a video to share on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, or another social network. You can also create a snapshot or report when that is more useful.

pageCta.title: Create a video and share your journey.
pageCta.body: Open Studio with a route file and prepare a video for your social networks, or use the quick guide for a short tour of the workspace.
